 LPG Cylinder Rules Change From November 1: Check New Rates, Refilling, Booking Company-Wise Revisions; Will Cooking Gas See Shortages in India?
 By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Oct 27, 2026, 19:24 IST Indane customers can use the IndianOil ONE app, Bharatgas customers can use HelloBPCL, and HP Gas customers can use HP PAY. Authentication can also be done through a distributor or during cylinder delivery.
 Eligible consumers who do not complete authentication may be unable to book subsidised refills 
 Numerous LPG-related rules and price updates will be closely watched from November 1, thus impacting domestic consumers, commercial establishments and households using Indane, HP Gas and Bharatgas. While monthly price revisions stay a key development, other crucial areas include Aadhaar-based authentication, refill booking intervals, delivery verification and the transition from LPG to piped natural gas (PNG). 
 Consumers should know that not every change discussed before November is a latest declared rule. Many requirements are already implemented and are slated to continue through the coming month. 
 What are LPG Distributors Protesting? 
 The LPG distributors in India are urging commission hikes from oil marketing companies (OMCs) due to overwork in executing new rules in LPG services since the US-Iran conflict began in late February. However, the Delhi police rejected protests on October 26, 2026, at CBD ground days after Jantar Mantar was denounced as a protest site. LPG distributors have threatened to conduct an indefinite strike. 
 The gas cylinder distributors had cautioned against conducting strikes at CBD ground on October 26, 2026. However, many LPG distributor federations have decided to distance themselves from the proposed protests and instead directly negotiate with OMCs and the Oil Ministry. The distributors urge higher commissions and relaxation of operational and commercial pressures due to the latest rules implemented in LPG services, thus forcing these distributors to overwork.
 What are LPG Distributors Protesting? 
 The LPG distributors in India are urging commission hikes from oil marketing companies (OMCs) due to overwork in executing new rules in LPG services since the US-Iran conflict began in late February. However, the Delhi police rejected protests on October 26, 2026, at CBD ground days after Jantar Mantar was denounced as a protest site. LPG distributors have threatened to conduct an indefinite strike.  
 The gas cylinder distributors had cautioned against conducting strikes at CBD ground on October 26, 2026. However, over 4,000 LPG distributor federations have decided to distance themselves from the proposed protests and instead directly negotiate with OMCs and the Oil Ministry. The distributors urge higher commissions and relaxation of operational and commercial pressures due to the latest rules implemented in LPG services, thus forcing these distributors to overwork. 
 Will there be LPGs Shortages? 
 They staged a protest in Delhi demanding a Rs 75 rise in distributor commissions, the implementation of compulsory PNG connection mandates, and relief from soaring operational costs. They have cautioned of an indefinite nationwide strike if demands are not fulfilled by November 25, 2026 
 Protests and strikes by LPG distributors and transporters in India may trigger localized or countrywide supply disruptions if unresolved, though massive distributor unions have recently issued ultimatums rather than an instant freeze. 
 Commercial and Domestic LPG Prices from November 1 
 Oil marketing companies generally review commercial LPG prices at the beginning of each month. The 19-kg cylinders, widely used by hotels, restaurants and other businesses, are especially sensitive to global energy prices and supply conditions. 
 According to Goodreturns, commercial cylinder prices rose in October. In Delhi, a 19-kg cylinder was priced at Rs 2,810, while rates varied across other cities. Any change effective November 1 will rely on the oil marketing companies' announcement.  
 Domestic LPG prices may follow a varied pattern. The 14.2-kg household cylinder had stayed unchanged since its previous revision on June 7, 2026, with the price in Delhi reported at Rs 942. Consumers should check the new city-wise rates before booking, as prices can differ by location. 
 Aadhaar e-KYC for Subsidised Refills 
 Biometric Aadhaar authentication is a crucial mandate for domestic consumers seeking refills at the regulated retail selling price with applicable subsidy. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas said that the requirement was implemented on October 1, 2026. Customers who have previously completed authentication do not need to repeat it.  
 Indane customers can use the IndianOil ONE app, Bharatgas customers can use HelloBPCL, and HP Gas customers can use HP PAY. Authentication can also be done through a distributor or during cylinder delivery. 
 Eligible consumers who do not complete authentication may be unable to book subsidised refills until the process is finished. Those who don’t authenticate can register that choice through their oil marketing company's available channels and may get LPG at market prices in 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders. 
 Although rising crude oil prices do not directly affect piped natural gas (PNG) prices in India, a lot depends on how much city-gas distributors' natural gas supply is from domestically produced gas versus imported liquefied natural gas (LNG). Also, government pricing rules, distribution costs and taxes are also added to the last price.

 4. What happens if Aadhaar e-KYC is not completed? 
 Situation 
 Impact on LPG refill 
 e-KYC completed 
 Eligible customers can book refills at the regulated retail selling price with applicable subsidy. 
 e-KYC not completed 
 Subsidised refill booking may be halted until authentication is completed. 
 Customer opts out of authentication 
 LPG may still be available at market price without subsidy, subject to applicable conditions and local availability. 
 Alternative cylinder option 
 The report cites 5 kg or 10 kg cylinders for customers who register their choice not to complete authentication. 
 Source: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and Goodreturns. Subsidy eligibility and availability depend on the applicable government and company rules.
